1. Plaintiff has sued the defendant seeking damages/compensation for the tort of malicious prosecution.

2. Shorn off unnecessary details, it is the case of plaintiff that an FIR bearing no. 524/13, PS Karawal Nagar, u/s 366/342/376/506/34 IPC Digitally CS No. 22/23 Shakir Vs. Rizwana signed by 1 of 7 AASHISH AASHISH GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2025.09.26 16:22:41 +0530 was registered against him on the basis of a complaint filed by the defendant (complainant therein) before the concerned Magistrate.
In the said matter, the plaintiff was arrested and matter was put to trial.

Consequently, after conclusion of trial, vide order dated 31.10.2022 passed by Ld. ASJ (SC-RC)-02, East,
KKD Court, plaintiff was acquitted of all the offences.
3. As per plaintiff, he and defendant had a love affair and they got married vide nikahnama dated 12.07.2013.
As per plaintiff, defendant was major at that time and consented for the said marriage.

Plaintiff claims that eventually, defendant made false and frivolous allegations of abduction, rape,
wrongful confinement and criminal intimidation before the concerned IO which led to his arrest and malicious prosecution in the said FIR.
Plaintiff was eventually acquitted in the said case.

Thus,
plaintiff is seeking compensation/damages from defendant for his malicious prosecution in the said case FIR (in which he was acquitted).
5.

Even though, plaintiff has given a very elaborate description of the events between the parties,
but, in sum and substance, plaintiff is relying on the copies of documents prepared by the IO along with copy of judgment of acquittal passed by Ld. ASJ for the purpose of this suit.
6. Since defendant did not appear and file any written statement, she was proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 25.10.2023.

10. The entire testimony of the plaintiff has gone unrebutted and unchallenged.

As per the judgment dated 31.10.2022 passed in FIR no. 524/13, PS Karawal Nagar, the concerned Sessions Court had opined that the defendant had gone with the plaintiff on her own accord and thereafter, performed marriage with him as per her own willingness and consent.

It further held that the allegations of abduction/rape are in contradiction to the circumstances shown on record and thus, acquitted the Shakir vs Rizwana on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131261842/
2 accused.
CS No. 22/23 Shakir Vs. Rizwana 3 of 7 11.
As per plaintiffs case, he suffered judicial custody of about eight months.
12. Thus, it is proved on record that plaintiff was maliciously prosecuted without any probable cause by defendant in the aforesaid case.
13. Thus, as far as the tort of malicious prosecution is concerned, the same is duly proved on record and thus, defendant is liable to compensate the plaintiff on the said count.
14. Now, a question arises as to how much money should plaintiff be awarded to the plaintiff.
Plaintiff has sought damages to the extent of Rs.20 lacs for malicious prosecution along with expenses made against court fees and legal expenses.
15. It is but obvious that in Indian society if a person is booked in a criminal case and that too under stringent provisions of rape, it would lead to loss of reputation to any given person.
The period for which the said person faces trial, each day would be a time when people in the society would put a question mark on his character leading to loss of reputation.
Again, such a person would also suffer mental agony, loss loss of job and legal expenses.
16. The plaintiff has not been cross-

examined at all by the defendant (who chose to remain ex-parte)
and thus, in effect, the entire testimony of the plaintiff has gone unrebutted and unchallenged.

It has been proved on record that the plaintiff was prosecuted without any probable cause and thus, he himself have suffered mentally and CS No. 22/23 Shakir Vs. Rizwana 4 of 7 physically from the date of filing of the FIR against him till he was eventually acquitted vide judgment dated 31.10.2022.

sentences.text: He even suffered incarceration for a period of about eight months.
A criminal trial that too under the provisions of rape etc must have broken the plaintiff internally and he himself have suffered grave mental torture on that count.
He must have visited the court multiple times during trial of the case and must have thus, suffered immense physical pain.

During the period when he visited the court,
he must have incurred legal expenses and would have also suffered financially because of loss of work for that day.
17. But, before awarding any compensation to the plaintiff, it has to be kept in mind that the compensation awarded is reasonable and should be compensatory in nature and not punitive.
18. In my humble opinion, for the loss of reputation and mental pain and suffering suffered by the plaintiff, a cumulative amount of Rs.5 lac would be reasonable.
This is considering the social and economic background of the parties.
Usually, for the loss of reputation and mental pain, no mathematical estimate can be made qua any person.
Thus, Courts are called upon to make a rough estimate of the loss suffered by a given party.
In this exercise, the social standing of the parties in society, their educational background and economic status may be relevant factors to come at a fair and reasonable assessment.

In this case, plaintiff is stated to be self-employed and is running a Shakir vs Rizwana on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131261842/
3 boutique.
Parties appear to come from similar social, economic and educational background.
This is considering the fact that plaintiff is CS No. 22/23 Shakir Vs. Rizwana 5 of 7 stated to have married the defendant and usually people of similar background enter into matrimony.
19. Considering the same, in my humble opinion, Rs. 5 lac appear to a fair and reasonable estimate of the loss suffered by plaintiff and thus, the same is awarded to him.
20. Plaintiff has also claimed damages on account of loss of livelihood.
As per his testimony, he remained in custody for about eight months.
Now, there is no evidence to show as to what was the earnings of the plaintiff in 2013 (when he was in custody).

Thus, if I treat plaintiff to be an skilled workman (he claiming to be a person who runs a boutique), the monthly wages for a skilled workman in Delhi effective from 01.10.2013 was Rs.9802/- per month.

Thus,
with defendant remaining in custody for a period of eight months would make him entitle to an amount of Rs.9802 x 8 = Rs.78,416/-.
21.
At the same time, cognizance can be taken of the fact that plaintiff was made to fight the false criminal case for almost a decade.

This would mean that as and when plaintiff must have been asked to appear in Court or before police, it is but obvious that he must have suffered financially as on that day he could not have fruitfully worked to earn any livelihood.

22. In such circumstances, an amount of Rs.1 lac plus the amount of Rs.
78,416/- appears to be a reasonable estimate of the loss of livelihood suffered by plaintiff.
Thus, in my humble opinion, for the loss of livelihood, plaintiff is found entitled to a sum of Rs.1,78,416/- for CS No. 22/23 Shakir Vs. Rizwana 6 of 7 the loss of livelihood suffered by him.
Accordingly, the said amount is awarded to plaintiff.
23. Again, plaintiff has also sought money for legal expenses suffered by him.
He has not led any specific evidence to show how much money did he expend on his defence.
24. As far as legal expenses are concerned, the amount of Rs.1 lac sought appears to be a reasonable estimate of the amount expended by plaintiff in fighting a false case foisted upon him.

Accordingly,
the said amount is also awarded to the plaintiff.
Conclusion 25.

In view of the above discussion, plaintiff is awarded a sum of Rs.7,78,416/- lacs (Rupees Seven Lac Seventy Eight Thousand Four Hundred and Sixteen only) to be recovered from the defendant as compensation for malicious prosecution.
26. Plaintiff is also entitled to cost of the present suit.
27. Accordingly, the present suit is decreed in aforesaid terms.
